topics.title: Introduction to CSS
topics.content:
Tutorials > Web Development > CSS > Basics

Introduction to CSS

Beginner ⏱️ 5 min read Updated: July 2026

CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) is a stylesheet language used to describe the presentation of a document written in HTML or XML. It defines how elements should be rendered on screen, on paper, in speech, or on other media.

Understanding Cascading

The term "Cascading" refers to the specific algorithm used by the browser to determine which style rules apply to an element when multiple rules conflict. It follows a hierarchy of priority, typically falling back from Inline styles > Internal/External stylesheets > Browser defaults.

Key Features of CSS

  • Separation of Concerns: Separates structure (HTML) from presentation (CSS).
  • Responsive Design: Allows creating websites that adapt to different screen sizes.
  • Reusability: One CSS file can style multiple HTML pages.
  • Maintainability: Easy to update the entire look of a website from a single file.

Advantages of CSS

Advantage Description
Faster Page Speed Less code means faster download times. Browsers cache external CSS files.
Superior Styles CSS offers far more styling capabilities than traditional HTML attributes.
Multiple Device Compatibility Styles can be customized for different devices (mobile, print, desktop).

CSS Syntax

A CSS rule-set consists of a selector and a declaration block:

CSS Syntax Structure
selector {
  property: value;
  another-property: another-value;
}

Example:

h1 {
  color: #10b981;
  font-size: 24px;
}

Here, h1 is the selector, color is the property, and #10b981 is the value.

topics.title: Styling HTML (Inline, Internal, External)
topics.content:
Tutorials > Web Development > CSS > Basics

Styling HTML: Inline, Internal & External CSS

Beginner ⏱️ 6 min read Updated: July 2026

CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) is used to style and format the layout of Web pages. There are three ways to insert CSS into an HTML document:

📌 Key Takeaways

  • Inline CSS: Applied directly inside an HTML element using the style attribute. Used for quick single-element overrides.
  • Internal CSS: Written inside a <style> block within the <head> section of the HTML file. Ideal for single-page documents.
  • External CSS: Defined in a separate .css file and linked using <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">. Best practice for maintainable websites.

1. Inline CSS Example

Syntax: Inline Style Attribute
<h1 style="color: #10b981; font-size: 24px; text-align: center;">Hello World</h1>

2. Internal CSS Example

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <style>
    body {
      background-color: #0f172a;
      color: #f8fafc;
    }
    .heading {
      color: #38bdf8;
      font-weight: bold;
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <h1 class="heading">Internal CSS Styling</h1>
</body>
</html>

3. External CSS Example

Link the external sheet inside HTML <head>:

<!-- index.html -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="css/main.css">

And write pure CSS rules inside main.css:

/* css/main.css */
.card {
  background: #1e293b;
  border-radius: 8px;
  padding: 20px;
  border: 1px solid #334155;
}
Visual Preview: Styles Comparison

topics.title: CSS Box Model (Margin, Padding, Border, Content)
topics.content:
Tutorials > Web Development > CSS > Basics

CSS Box Model: Margin, Padding, Border & Content

Core Concept ⏱️ 8 min read Updated: July 2026

All HTML elements can be considered as boxes. In CSS, the term Box Model is used when talking about design and layout. It wraps around every HTML element and consists of four layers.

📦 Box Model Architecture

  • Content: The real content of the element, where text and images appear.
  • Padding: Clears an area around the content. Padding is inside the border and is transparent.
  • Border: A border that goes around the padding and content.
  • Margin: Clears an area outside the border. Margin is completely transparent and separates elements.
Box Model Breakdown Diagram
MARGIN (Outer spacing)
BORDER (Element boundary)
PADDING (Inner spacing)
CONTENT (Text / Images / Elements)

CSS Box Sizing: content-box vs border-box

/* Standard CSS Reset rule */
*, *::before, *::after {
  box-sizing: border-box; /* Includes padding and border in total width/height */
}

.box {
  width: 300px;
  padding: 20px;
  border: 5px solid #10b981;
  margin: 15px;
}

💡 Pro Tip

Always set box-sizing: border-box globally. Without it, adding padding or borders increases the actual element width beyond your specified width property!

topics.title: CSS Selectors & Specificity
topics.content:
Tutorials > Web Development > CSS > Basics

CSS Selectors & Specificity Hierarchy

Essential ⏱️ 10 min read Updated: July 2026

CSS Selectors target HTML elements to apply styles. When multiple conflicting rules apply to an element, CSS uses Specificity rules to decide which style wins.

Types of CSS Selectors

Selector Type Syntax Example Description
Universal * Selects all HTML elements on the page.
Element / Tag p, h1, div Selects all elements with the specified tag name.
Class Selector .btn, .card Selects elements with the specified class attribute.
ID Selector #header, #main Selects a single unique element with the specified ID.
Attribute Selector [type="text"] Selects elements based on an attribute or attribute value.
Pseudo-Class :hover, :nth-child(2) Selects elements based on state or DOM position.
Pseudo-Element ::before, ::after Styles specific parts of an element or injects content.

CSS Specificity Hierarchy Score

📊 Specificity Calculation (Inline > ID > Class > Tag)

  1. Inline Style: (1, 0, 0, 0) - Highest weight (e.g. style="...")
  2. ID Selectors: (0, 1, 0, 0) - (e.g. #navbar)
  3. Classes, Attributes, Pseudo-classes: (0, 0, 1, 0) - (e.g. .btn:hover)
  4. Elements & Pseudo-elements: (0, 0, 0, 1) - (e.g. h1::first-letter)

Note: !important overrides all normal specificity rules. Use sparingly!

/* Specificity Example */
p { color: white; }                  /* (0,0,0,1) */
.text-green { color: #10b981; }      /* (0,0,1,0) - Wins over tag */
#main-text { color: #38bdf8; }       /* (0,1,0,0) - Wins over class */

/* Attribute & Pseudo-class */
input[type="submit"]:hover {
  background-color: #059669;
}

topics.title: CSS Combinators
topics.content:
Tutorials > Web Development > CSS > Basics

CSS Combinators: Relationships Between Elements

Intermediate ⏱️ 7 min read Updated: July 2026

A combinator explains the relationship between selectors. CSS includes four different combinator types to target nested or sibling elements precisely.

The 4 CSS Combinators

Combinator Name Symbol Rule Example Matching Description
Descendant Combinator (space) div p Matches all <p> elements inside a <div>, regardless of nesting depth.
Child Combinator > div > p Matches only direct children <p> elements immediately inside <div>.
Adjacent Sibling + h2 + p Matches the single <p> element directly after an <h2>.
General Sibling ~ h2 ~ p Matches all <p> elements that are siblings following an <h2>.

Combinator Code Example

/* 1. Descendant */
.container span {
  color: #fbbf24; /* Targets all spans inside .container */
}

/* 2. Direct Child */
.menu > li {
  display: inline-block; /* Targets only top-level li items */
}

/* 3. Adjacent Sibling */
h2 + p {
  font-size: 1.1rem;
  font-weight: 600; /* First paragraph after H2 */
}

/* 4. General Sibling */
.active ~ .item {
  opacity: 0.7; /* All subsequent sibling .item elements */
}

topics.title: Styling Images
topics.content:
Tutorials > Web Development > CSS > Elements & Properties

Styling Images: Responsive Layouts & Object Fit

Practical ⏱️ 6 min read Updated: July 2026

Images play a crucial role in modern responsive UI design. Key properties include object-fit, aspect-ratio, borders, shadows, and hover scale effects.

Key Image Properties

  • max-width: 100%: Prevents images from overflowing parent containers.
  • object-fit: cover: Crops and scales images cleanly to fit containers without distortion.
  • aspect-ratio: 16 / 9: Preserves explicit proportions across screens.
  • filter: Applies visual adjustments like grayscale(), blur(), or drop-shadow().
/* Responsive Card Image */
.card-img {
  width: 100%;
  height: 220px;
  object-fit: cover;
  border-radius: 8px;
  box-shadow: 0 10px 25px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4);
  transition: transform 0.4s ease, filter 0.4s ease;
}

.card-img:hover {
  transform: scale(1.03);
  filter: brightness(1.1);
}

topics.title: Audio & Video Elements
topics.content:
Tutorials > Web Development > CSS > Elements & Properties

Styling HTML5 Audio & Video Elements

Media UI ⏱️ 5 min read Updated: July 2026

HTML5 <audio> and <video> elements can be styled with custom borders, responsive fluid wrappers, aspect ratio boxes, and controls overlays.

Responsive Video Wrapper Pattern

/* Fluid 16:9 Video Container */
.video-container {
  position: relative;
  width: 100%;
  aspect-ratio: 16 / 9;
  border-radius: 12px;
  overflow: hidden;
  border: 1px solid #334155;
  box-shadow: 0 20px 40px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6);
}

.video-container video {
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
  object-fit: cover;
}

/* Audio Player Custom Styling */
audio {
  width: 100%;
  accent-color: #10b981; /* Styles native browser media controls */
  border-radius: 30px;
}

topics.title: Styling Tables
topics.content:
Tutorials > Web Development > CSS > Elements & Properties

Styling HTML Tables: Borders, Zebra Striping & Responsiveness

Data UI ⏱️ 7 min read Updated: July 2026

Default HTML tables look plain. CSS transforms tables into clean, readable data grids using border-collapse, cell padding, zebra-striping, hover states, and responsive scroll wrappers.

.custom-table {
  width: 100%;
  border-collapse: collapse;
  margin-top: 1rem;
  font-size: 0.95rem;
}

.custom-table th {
  background-color: #1e293b;
  color: #10b981;
  padding: 12px 16px;
  text-align: left;
  border-bottom: 2px solid #334155;
}

.custom-table td {
  padding: 12px 16px;
  border-bottom: 1px solid #334155;
}

/* Zebra Striping */
.custom-table tbody tr:nth-child(even) {
  background-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.02);
}

/* Row Hover Effect */
.custom-table tbody tr:hover {
  background-color: rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.1);
}
Visual Preview: Styled Data Table
ID Property Default Value Status
01 border-collapse separate Active
02 box-sizing content-box Overridden

topics.title: Styling Forms
topics.content:
Tutorials > Web Development > CSS > Elements & Properties

Styling Forms: Inputs, Focus States & Custom Buttons

Interactive UI ⏱️ 8 min read Updated: July 2026

Form controls require careful CSS styling for optimal user experience (UX) and accessibility. Focus rings, placeholder text, validation highlights, and submit buttons should respond to user action smoothly.

/* Form Input Styling */
.form-input {
  width: 100%;
  padding: 12px 16px;
  background: #0f172a;
  border: 1px solid #334155;
  border-radius: 6px;
  color: #f8fafc;
  font-size: 1rem;
  transition: border-color 0.3s, box-shadow 0.3s;
}

/* Accessible Focus Outline */
.form-input:focus {
  outline: none;
  border-color: #10b981;
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.25);
}

/* Form Button */
.btn-submit {
  background: linear-gradient(135deg, #10b981, #059669);
  color: white;
  padding: 12px 24px;
  border: none;
  border-radius: 6px;
  font-weight: 600;
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: transform 0.2s, box-shadow 0.2s;
}

.btn-submit:hover {
  transform: translateY(-2px);
  box-shadow: 0 8px 20px rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.4);
}

topics.title: CSS Positioning (Static, Relative, Absolute, Fixed, Sticky)
topics.content:
Tutorials > Web Development > CSS > Positioning

CSS Positioning: Static, Relative, Absolute, Fixed & Sticky

Layout Engine ⏱️ 9 min read Updated: July 2026

The position property specifies the type of positioning method used for an element (static, relative, absolute, fixed, or sticky).

Position Value Behavior Description Offset Properties Supported
static Default position. Elements render in normal document flow. No (top, left, etc. ignored)
relative Positioned relative to its normal position without removing it from flow. Yes (top, right, bottom, left)
absolute Removed from flow. Positioned relative to nearest positioned ancestor (non-static). Yes (top, right, bottom, left)
fixed Removed from flow. Positioned relative to viewport; stays in place during scroll. Yes (top, right, bottom, left)
sticky Toggles between relative and fixed depending on scroll position. Yes (e.g. top: 0)

Positioning Code Example

/* Parent relative container */
.card-container {
  position: relative;
  width: 300px;
  height: 200px;
  background: #1e293b;
}

/* Absolute Badge positioned at top right */
.badge-top {
  position: absolute;
  top: 10px;
  right: 10px;
  background: #ef4444;
  color: white;
  padding: 4px 10px;
  border-radius: 20px;
  font-size: 0.75rem;
}

/* Sticky Header */
.sticky-nav {
  position: sticky;
  top: 0;
  z-index: 1000;
  background: #0f172a;
}

topics.title: Display Types (Block, Inline, Inline-Block, None)
topics.content:
Tutorials > Web Development > CSS > Display & Layout

CSS Display Property: Block, Inline, Inline-Block & None

Foundations ⏱️ 6 min read Updated: July 2026

The display property is the most important CSS property for controlling layout. It determines how an element renders in the document tree.

🔍 Display Values Overview

  • block: Starts on a new line and takes up full width (e.g., <div>, <p>, <h1>). Accepts width, height, margins, and paddings.
  • inline: Does not start on a new line, takes only required width (e.g., <span>, <a>). Does NOT respect top/bottom width, height, or vertical margins!
  • inline-block: Formatted like an inline element, but accepts width, height, padding, and margin properties.
  • none: Hides element completely; removes it from document layout flow.
.nav-item {
  display: inline-block; /* Inline horizontal flow with custom width/padding */
  width: 120px;
  padding: 10px;
  text-align: center;
}

.hidden-element {
  display: none; /* Completely invisible & occupies no space */
}

topics.title: CSS Flexbox Layout
topics.content:
Tutorials > Web Development > CSS > Display & Layout

CSS Flexbox: 1D Flexible Box Layout Model

Modern Layout ⏱️ 10 min read Updated: July 2026

Flexbox (Flexible Box Layout) is designed to provide a more efficient way to lay out, align, and distribute space among items in a container, even when their size is dynamic or unknown.

Key Flexbox Container Properties
.flex-container {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: row;        /* row | column | row-reverse | column-reverse */
  justify-content: space-between; /* flex-start | flex-end | center | space-between | space-around */
  align-items: center;        /* flex-start | flex-end | center | baseline | stretch */
  flex-wrap: wrap;            /* nowrap | wrap | wrap-reverse */
  gap: 1.5rem;                /* Gap spacing between flex items */
}

Flex Item Properties

.flex-item {
  flex-grow: 1;    /* Ability for flex item to grow if necessary */
  flex-shrink: 0;  /* Ability for flex item to shrink */
  flex-basis: 250px; /* Default size before remaining space is distributed */
  align-self: flex-end; /* Overrides container align-items for single item */
}

topics.title: CSS Grid Layout
topics.content:
Tutorials > Web Development > CSS > Display & Layout

CSS Grid: 2D Grid-Based Layout System

Modern Layout ⏱️ 11 min read Updated: July 2026

CSS Grid Layout is the most powerful 2-dimensional layout system in CSS. It handles both columns and rows simultaneously.

Responsive Grid Without Media Queries

.grid-container {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr));
  gap: 20px;
}

.grid-card {
  background: #1e293b;
  padding: 24px;
  border-radius: 10px;
  border: 1px solid #334155;
}

Explicit Grid Areas

.page-layout {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-areas:
    "header header"
    "sidebar main"
    "footer footer";
  grid-template-columns: 250px 1fr;
}

.header  { grid-area: header; }
.sidebar { grid-area: sidebar; }
.main    { grid-area: main; }
.footer  { grid-area: footer; }

topics.title: CSS Transitions & Transforms
topics.content:
Tutorials > Web Development > CSS > Animations

CSS Transitions & 2D/3D Transforms

Interactive ⏱️ 7 min read Updated: July 2026

CSS transitions allow property changes in CSS values to occur smoothly over a specified duration. Transforms rotate, scale, skew, or translate elements in 2D or 3D space.

Transition Properties

.button {
  background-color: #10b981;
  transform: scale(1);
  /* shorthand: property duration timing-function delay */
  transition: background-color 0.3s ease, transform 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);
}

.button:hover {
  background-color: #059669;
  transform: scale(1.05) translateY(-3px);
}

Transform Functions

  • translate(x, y): Moves element from current position.
  • scale(x, y): Increases or decreases element size.
  • rotate(deg): Rotates element clockwise or counter-clockwise.
  • skew(x-angle, y-angle): Skews element along X and Y axes.

topics.title: CSS Keyframes Animation
topics.content:
Tutorials > Web Development > CSS > Animations

CSS Keyframe Animations & @keyframes Rules

Advanced FX ⏱️ 8 min read Updated: July 2026

An animation lets an element gradually change from one style to another. You can change as many CSS properties as you want, as many times as you want, using @keyframes rules.

@keyframes Declaration
@keyframes pulseGlow {
  0% {
    transform: scale(1);
    box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.7);
  }
  50% {
    transform: scale(1.05);
    box-shadow: 0 0 20px 10px rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.3);
  }
  100% {
    transform: scale(1);
    box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 rgba(16, 185, 129, 0);
  }
}

.glowing-badge {
  animation: pulseGlow 2s infinite ease-in-out;
}

topics.title: Pseudo Elements & Classes
topics.content:
Tutorials > Web Development > CSS > Advanced

Advanced Pseudo-Elements (::before, ::after) & Pseudo-Classes

Advanced ⏱️ 8 min read Updated: July 2026

Pseudo-classes target elements in specific states (e.g. :nth-child(), :not(), :focus-within), while Pseudo-elements style specific sub-parts or inject decorative elements into the DOM without extra HTML tags.

/* Injecting decorative gradient line using ::after */
.section-title {
  position: relative;
  display: inline-block;
  margin-bottom: 2rem;
}

.section-title::after {
  content: '';
  position: absolute;
  bottom: -8px;
  left: 0;
  width: 60%;
  height: 3px;
  background: linear-gradient(90deg, #10b981, transparent);
  border-radius: 2px;
}

/* Target structural nth-child */
.list-item:nth-child(odd) {
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.03);
}

/* Target elements NOT matching selector */
.btn:not(.btn-disabled):hover {
  cursor: pointer;
}

topics.title: Media Queries & Responsive Design
topics.content:
Tutorials > Web Development > CSS > Advanced

Media Queries (@media) & Mobile-First Responsive Design

Responsive ⏱️ 9 min read Updated: July 2026

Media queries are a key feature of CSS3 that allow content rendering to adapt to conditions such as screen resolution, viewport width, device orientation, and color scheme preferences.

📱 Common Breakpoint Standard

  • 320px - 480px: Mobile devices
  • 481px - 768px: iPads & Tablets
  • 769px - 1024px: Laptops & Small Screens
  • 1025px - 1200px+: Desktops & Large Displays
/* Mobile-First Approach: Base styles for mobile */
.sidebar {
  display: none; /* Hidden on narrow screens */
}

/* Tablet & Desktop breakpoint override */
@media (min-width: 768px) {
  .sidebar {
    display: block;
    width: 280px;
  }
  
  .main-content {
    margin-left: 280px;
  }
}

/* Dark / Light Preference detection */
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  body {
    background-color: #0f172a;
    color: #f8fafc;
  }
}

topics.title: Z-Index & Stacking Context
topics.content:
Tutorials > Web Development > CSS > Advanced

Z-Index Property & Stacking Context Hierarchy

Depth Engine ⏱️ 7 min read Updated: July 2026

The z-index property specifies the stack order of an element. An element with greater stack order is always in front of an element with a lower stack order.

⚠️ Important Rule

z-index ONLY works on positioned elements (e.g. position: relative, absolute, fixed, or sticky) and flex/grid child items!

.modal-backdrop {
  position: fixed;
  top: 0;
  left: 0;
  width: 100vw;
  height: 100vh;
  background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.75);
  z-index: 999; /* Under dialog, above page */
}

.modal-dialog {
  position: fixed;
  top: 50%;
  left: 50%;
  transform: translate(-50%, -50%);
  z-index: 1000; /* Highest priority layer */
}

topics.title: Bootstrap Overview
topics.content:
Tutorials > Web Development > CSS > Frameworks

Bootstrap Framework: Grid System & Utility Classes

Framework ⏱️ 10 min read Updated: July 2026

Bootstrap is the world's most popular front-end open-source toolkit. It features a 12-column responsive flexbox grid system, extensive prebuilt components, and powerful utility classes.

12-Column Responsive Grid System

<div class="container">
  <div class="row">
    <div class="col-12 col-md-8">
      <h2>Main Content (8 cols on desktop, 12 on mobile)</h2>
    </div>
    <div class="col-12 col-md-4">
      <aside>Sidebar (4 cols on desktop)</aside>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

Bootstrap vs Pure Custom CSS Comparison

Feature Bootstrap Framework Pure Custom CSS
Development Speed ⚡ Rapid prototyping using ready components 🛠️ Custom built from ground up
File Size & Control Includes framework overhead unless purged Zero overhead, 100% granular design control
Consistency Standardized design tokens across teams Requires custom design system rules
